the reason why capitalism feels like it's not working well anymore in the US

is because people don't credibly believe they can get ahead anymore

conspicuously, a lot of the opportunities to do this with local small businesses in local communities have been bought up by private equity. almost any cash flowing, local business has been bought up by private equity, whose goal is to corner the market on everything from bowling alleys to car washes to veterinary care to funeral homes

it doesn't mean there are no opportunities left, but they are substantially fewer and harder for people to picture themselves in

alternatively, you have the corporate route which is also simultaneously being gutted for new hires

meanwhile, people with wealth and power can trivially compound it in markets which feel like they are rigged and public systems which are being max extracted from by political actors in unprecedented ways

the system won't work / can't work if people at least don't FEEL like they can get ahead

they need that belief in order to be willing to grind it out. once that believe dies, especially with younger generations entering the workforce, then you've got a serious problem

and that's the core socio-economic problem we're wrestling with today
